RESULT 15/07/26

Implementation: Update Search Published Folder Bookmark API

Example API

Endpoint: GET /search/folder-bookmark/published

Retrieves publicly published folder bookmarks from all creators. The endpoint supports pagination, full-text search and category filtering for the Bookmark tab in Search Discover.

Request parameters

  • page (int, optional): page number; default 1.
  • limit (int, optional): item count; default 8.
  • q (string, optional): folder-name keyword; name is a backward-compatible alias.
  • category (int, optional): category_id; 0 or omitted skips the filter.
  • include (string, optional): comma-separated output fields.

Response contract

Each item contains the folder header fields slug, name, description, location, location_name, category_name, published_at, total_bookmark, thumbnail, potd, and user.

The nested user object includes username, fullname, avatar, and encrypt. The compatible total shape remains:

{ "counter_bookmak": 19 }

Update API Search Published Folder Bookmark Implementation

Summary

Updated /search/folder-bookmark/published to provide all folder/header data required by the published-folder detail page. The frontend can pass folder data from search results and request /bookmark/published/:slug only for posts and totals.

  • Unsupported roles return 401 Unauthorized.

published_at, total_bookmark, thumbnail, owner_username, owner_fullname,
owner_avatar, owner_encrypt

This remains intentional when include is sent because internal response formatting needs these fields.

Filtering and compatibility

  • User role also excludes blocked owners.
  • Existing q/name, category, page, limit, include, ec, and sl behavior remains.
  • include filters the final response, not the internal data requirements.
  • total_bookmark keeps { "counter_bookmak": 19 } compatibility.

Goal

Make /search/folder-bookmark/published return the folder fields needed by the frontend detail page, avoiding a redundant folder-header request after navigation.

Example API

Endpoint: GET /bookmark/published/:slug
Description: Retrieves paginated posts inside a published folder bookmark. This endpoint returns only post list data and dynamic totals. Folder/header data should come from GET /search/folder-bookmark/published.

Example cURL Request

  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  -H "ec: false" \
  --data-urlencode "page=1" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=10"

Request Parameters

  • page (int, optional): Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1.
  • limit (int, optional): Number of posts per page. Defaults to 10.

Visibility Rules

  • Role viewer can access public published folder posts.
  • Role user can access public published folder posts.
  • Other roles return 401 Unauthorized.
  • All roles exclude:
    • deactive users
    • private/non-public posts
    • unpublished posts
    • video360 posts
  • Role user also excludes:
    • blocked users
    • blocked posts

issues.display_title: Issue #459: Update List POTD and Detail POTD
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/07/26

✅ Implementation: Broadcast Viewer Access

Overview

This implementation updates the broadcast notification APIs so the viewer role can access public broadcast and POTD data without requiring a full user profile lookup.

Previously these actions assumed a logged-in user role and called UserFunctions.UserDatas(c, encrypt). That fails for viewer because the auth middleware assigns viewer requests a generated encrypt value and an empty userId.

Routes Updated

  • GET /notification/list-broadcast
  • GET /notification/list-potd
  • GET /notification/list-broadcast-bookmark/:slug
  • GET /notification/detail-broadcast-post/:slug

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcast.go
  2. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go
  3. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcastBookmark.go
  4. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/DetailBroadcastPost.go

Technical Details

1. Role Validation

Some API updated action now accepts both roles:

if role != "user" && role != "viewer" {

	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")

}

This keeps non-broadcast roles blocked while allowing viewer access.

2. Viewer-safe User Data Handling

The UserDatas lookup now runs only for role == "user":

if role == "user" {

	userData := UserFunctions.UserDatas(c, encrypt)
	// load last_login and user-specific block lists

}

For viewer, the endpoint skips user profile lookup and uses a generated lastLogin timestamp for encrypted response metadata.

3. Filtering Behavior

All roles still apply the global deactivated-user filter:

notInEncrypt = deactiveUser

For user, the endpoint also appends user-specific blocked users and blocked posts where supported:

notInEncrypt = append(deactiveUser, blockUser...)

This keeps the existing logged-in user privacy behavior while making viewer requests independent from user-specific Redis keys.

4. Support-only Filter

The sp=true support-personal filter remains restricted. Viewer requests with sp=true return unauthorized because viewer has no real user profile or support email:

if role == "viewer" {

	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")

}

5. Encrypted Response Shape

The ec == "true" branch now follows a single-return pattern. It replaces responses with the encrypted payload, adds e4 for viewer requests, and returns once at the end:

if ec == "true" {

	MySecret, _ := Functions.KeyEncrypt(lastLogin, encrypt)
	rowDatasSlice := []interface{}{MySecret, lastLogin, 0, responses}
	encText, _ := Functions.EncryptResult(rowDatasSlice, "success", true, 200)
	responses = map[string]interface{}{
		"messages": "...",
		"cry":      encText,
		"ls":       Functions.EpochTime(lastLogin),
	}
	if role == "viewer" {
		responses["e4"] = encrypt
	}
}

return c.Status(fiber.StatusOK).JSON(responses)

Backward Compatibility

  • Existing user role behavior remains unchanged for block filters and encrypted responses.
  • Existing route paths and query parameters remain unchanged.
  • Viewer access is limited to public broadcast data. User-specific filters are skipped only because viewer has no user account context.
  • sp=true remains unavailable to viewer.

Verification

go test ./...

Result: passed.

  • /notification/detail-broadcast-post/:slug
